metadata_caption: USA’s most scenic road?! DETAILS ⬇️😍 📍 The Zion-Mount Carmel Road in Zion National Park, Utah is a scenic 25-mile stretch connecting Zion National Park, Grand Canyon National Park, and Bryce Canyon National Park, showcasing the stunning red rock canyons and cliffs that make these national parks famous. 🌄 Along this unforgettable drive, you’ll pass through towering sandstone formations, slickrock canyons, and the historic 1.1-mile Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel. At the time of its completion, in 1930, the Zion-Mt. Carmel Tunnel was the longest in the world and is still considered an engineering marvel to this day!  🛣️ No reservation is currently required to drive this road, but vehicles over 11’4” in height or 7’10” in width (including mirrors) will need an escort to pass through the Zion Tunnel, available for a fee during set hours. Check nps.gov for details on tunnel restrictions and traffic conditions. 🌅 This spectacular drive is one of the best ways to see Zion National Park! We’ve driven it multiple times during day trips to Bryce Canyon National Park and have been stunned every single time. We recommend driving it early or later in the day to avoid heavy traffic and catch the red cliffs glowing in the soft morning or evening light. 💌 Send this to someone who needs to take this drive with you!
